reference.title: Barbell Forward Backward Lunge (male)
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as you step and lower, breathe out as you drive up; re-brace as the foot passes under you.
breathing.cadence: About 3.5 s for the forward lunge and 3.5 s for the reverse lunge, without stopping in between

prescription.reps: 6-10 per leg (one rep = forward and back)
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and lighter than a static lunge: balance limits it. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Heavier bar, then a short pause at the bottom of each half.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down. Stand tall, feet hip width.
Take a long step forward with the right foot, land heel first, back heel rolling up.
Drop straight down until the front knee is about 90 degrees and the back knee is just above the floor; trunk tall.
Push off the front heel and bring the right foot back under the hip without stopping.
Keep going: reach the same foot straight back and land on its ball.
Lower again, now with the left as the front leg, front shin about vertical.
Drive through the left heel and step the right foot back in.

mistakes.mistake: Stepping too short so the front heel lifts
mistakes.fix: Step long enough that the front shin is about vertical at the bottom.

mistakes.mistake: Losing balance as the foot passes under the body
mistakes.fix: Slow the swing and brace; the foot travels close to the floor.
Stop just above the floor and control each descent.
Keep the chest up and the bar over the middle of the base.

kinematics.setup: Feet hip width (18 cm), side by side
kinematics.peak: Forward: right ankle 80 cm ahead; backward: right ankle 80 cm behind the left
kinematics.norm: About one leg length forward or back (Song 2023, split squat); the front shin near vertical at the bottom (common guideline)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Left ≈102° (14 cm up) in the forward half; right ≈94° (13 cm up) in the backward half
kinematics.norm: Lowers to just above the floor, about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upright to a slight forward lean; forward and reverse lunges load the joints differently (Park 2016; Hoogenboom 2024)

kinematics.peak: Forward lunge 3.4 s (step 0.8, down 1.0, pause 0.3, up 0.75, push back 0.5), straight into the reverse lunge 3.7 s, 0.85 s reset

cautions: Take the bar from a rack at about shoulder height; use clear floor space in front and behind.
Start light: the moving base makes balance the limit.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance issues: do the forward and reverse halves as separate reps, or hold dumbbells instead.
Knee pain: shorter range, or the reverse half only.
progressions: Pause at the bottom of each half.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors control each descent and drive each rise; the forward step adds a braking load at landing (Park 2016).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors control each descent and drive each rise; the forward step adds a braking load at landing (Park 2016).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; the reverse lunge places relatively more demand on the hip than the forward lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; the reverse lunge places relatively more demand on the hip than the forward lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension of the front leg.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension of the front leg.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Control the front ankle and push off the front foot to step back.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the front ankle and push off the front foot to step back.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the foot on one leg.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the foot on one leg.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk upright under the bar while the base changes.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Part of the brace; resist sway as the feet move.

muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat under the bar.
